newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU eyes Canal Plus EBU link.
newsitem.headline: EU eyes Canal Plus EBU link.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert hinted on Thursday that French pay-television channel Canal Plus would be excluded from rules allowing public broadcasters to pool forces to negotiate exclusive sports rights.
Speaking at a conference on public services, Van Miert reiterated recent comments that it was only fair that state-controlled TV channels united forces against large private media groups.
But he thought that the public broadcasters grouped in the Gebeva-based European Broadcasting Union (EBU) had made a mistake by teaming up with Canal Plus.

"In principle, we have no objection against public broadcasters organising themselves to negotiate sports rights...but they made the mistake of admitting Canal Plus which is not public," he told the conference organised by the European Parliament.

In July, the European Court of Justice annulled a Commission decision of June 1993 which granted EBU an exemption from competition rules when acquiring exclusive rights to sports events. The court argued that the decision had not been substantiated and noted the presence of Canal Plus and France's TF1 despite the latter having been privatised in the mid 80s.
Van Miert did not mention TF1. Last month he said the Commission would restate EBU's sports TV rights.
EBU groups 67 European radio and television organisations. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
